title: Modular SDKenV learning pathways v0
content:
Purpose: capture a minimal, modular learning path for new integrators and internal teammates that teaches the Redwood SDK surface, common failure modes, instrumentation, and a small set of hands-on labs. This is intentionally lightweight and split into 6 independent modules so teams can pick the modules that match their onboarding window (10m, 1hr, 3hr, half-day).

Audience: new engineers (frontend/backend), solutions engineers, internal support who need a repeatable, measurable ramp. Emphasis on first 60 minutes that produce an instrumented sample request hitting hosted API and a local simulated fallback.

High-level principles (working):
- Small, safe wins: every module ends with a single test that proves the learning objective.
- Modular: each module can be consumed independently (lablet), or composed into a 3-4 hour bootcamp.
- Observable by default: telemetry hooks, synthetic telemetry checks, and 2 simple SLOs included in each module.
- Failure-resilient: show common error surface and defensive patterns early.
- Minimal friction: pre-seeded sandbox code + disposable credentials.

Module index (6 micro-modules):
1) Orientation & quickwire (10m)
   - Goal: make a single authenticated request to Redwood hosted inference from a Node/HTTP client and inspect tokens/latency from the Console.
   - Artifacts: small node script, curl sample, checklist: API key, project id, region.
   - Smoke test: successful 200 with streaming header + token count in Console within 60s.

2) Local dev loop & stubbed mode (30-45m)
   - Goal: run SDK in local stubbed mode (no network) and assert deterministic outputs for unit tests.
   - Lab: local mock server that mirrors Redwood response shapes; example jest tests.
   - Notes: how to switch between hosted, dedicated, and private endpoints via env var.

3) Prompt safety + cost playground (45-60m)
   - Goal: teach token budgeting, stop sequences, response truncation and a simple reranking flow to reduce token spend.
   - Exercises: profile prompt token counts, implement prefix caching example, run an embed+search combo.
   - Check: run a small script that reports cost delta after applying caching.

4) Observability & regression signals (1hr)
   - Goal: wire minimal telemetry (request id, tokens, latencies, model, route) into sample app; create a synthetic check that fails on regression (latency increase or token blowup).
   - Implementation hints: use provided telemetry client in sdk-examples; sample tracing snippet and Console dashboard URL.
   - Failure modes to demonstrate: KV cache misses, tokenization spikes, model fallback events.

5) Failure handling & fallback matrix (30-45m)
   - Goal: implement simple fallbacks (region fallback, model variant fallback, cached response) and a circuit-breaker wrapper for high error-rate periods.
   - Lab: add a resilient caller wrapper with exponential backoff + canary route.
   - Test: simulate model-unavailable and confirm fallback path returns within SLO.

6) Embedded evaluation + quick A/B rollout (1hr)
   - Goal: run a minimal eval (10 prompts) against two model variants and use the Console rollout API to split traffic.
   - Exercise: script that collects responses, computes simple ngram BLEU-ish score and flips a rollout percentage.

Pedagogy: each module includes:
- "Why this matters" short note (1 paragraph)
- 3 concrete steps (what to run, where to look)
- A one-line smoke test (pass/fail)
- 2 common pitfalls and how to recover
- A link to a reproducible code snippet in sdk-examples repo

Minimum sandbox contents to ship with newcomer experience:
- seed-credentials (ephemeral) and README on rotation policy
- node/python samples for orientation and stubbed mode
- telemetry helper library with README and two example dashboards (latency + tokens)
- small mock server (docker-compose) for local-only labs

Instrumentation and metrics (suggested):
- request.count, request.error.count, request.latency.p95, tokens.generated.sum, fallback.count, cache.hit.percent
- synthetic probe that runs the 10-prompt eval once per hour and alerts on score regression > 8%

Success metrics for this curriculum (proposed):
- 80% of new devs can complete Module 1 & 2 in first 60 minutes without help
- Median time to first instrumented request <= 25 minutes
- Reduction in first-week support tickets related to "how to retry/fallback" by 40% after adoption

Open questions / decision points (notes-to-self):
- Do we require a sandbox org per region or is a single multi-region sandbox enough for onboarding? (concerning Dedicated behavior)
- How opinionated should fallback patterns be in the examples? We want safe defaults but avoid coupling teams to them.
- Which telemetry storage class to recommend by default (retention 7d vs 30d) for new customers?

Implementation next steps (rough):
- Week 1: seed repo + minimal README + Module 1 artifacts (Asha)
- Week 2: Module 2 + mock server + tests (Diego)
- Week 3: Observability templates + Console dashboard links (Priya)
- Week 4: Failure patterns + evaluation scripts + publish interal beta

References / links:
- SDK examples repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples
- Console rollout docs: https://confluence.redwood/rollouts (placeholder)
- JIRA ticket for curriculum epic: DEVEXP-987

Notes to self (scrappy):
- Keep labs focused: 1 small change -> 1 measurable delta. Avoid long multi-step labs that block.
- Add a short "trainer cheat sheet" with common Q&A and demo scripts for SEs.
- Consider pairing the 1-hour lab with a short 10-slide "why this matters" deck for PM/PD demos.

Scratch ideas (future):
- Short badge/cert: "Redwood SDK Fundamentals" after passing automated smoke tests for Modules 1-4.
- Tiny interactive web runner embedded in docs for Module 1 (run a single request against a sandboxed API key)

End of draft - feedback welcome.
